sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal by appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act.

1988 is arising out of the Award dated 10-01-2023 passed by Member, Second Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ujjain (hereinafter it would be referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 452 of 2020 seeking enhancement of compensation amount.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.
3.

As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, for the death of Omprakash (husband of appellant No.1- herein), the Claims Tribunal after assessing the income of deceased at Rs.6000/- per month,
applying 10% towards future prospects and applying multiplier of 9 including filial consortium,
funeral and loss of estate, has awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,11,600/- along-with NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35296 2 MA-2718-2023 interest in favour of Claimants from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants contends that Claims Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Claims Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.6,000/- per month.

As per the evidence came on record, he was a mason by Smt. Badambai vs Raju on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2493538/
1 profession.

However, accepting earning of deceased as Rs.7,950/- per month in view of the Minimum Wages Act and adding future prospects, applying adequate multiplier including compensation under other conventional heads, the reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned Award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case, which does not call for any interference by this Court.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellants.
So far as income of the deceased is concerned, as per the evidence that came on record, he was a mason, therefore, in view of Minimum Wages Act, his income should be assessed as Rs.7,950/- per month.
Therefore, his income is fixed as Rs.7,950/- per month instead of Rs.6,000/- per month as assessed by the Claims Tribunal.

8. It is needless to mention here that appellant No.1 is the wife, appellant No.2 is daughter of deceased and appellants No.3 and 4 are sons of deceased, therefore, they are entitled to get towards loss of filial consortium @ Rs.44,000/- each.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35296 3 MA-2718-2023 9.

In view of above, the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is modified as under:
 HEAD AM  Monthly income Rs.7,950/-
 Future prospects 10 %
 Loss of dependency 1/4th  Multiplier 9 Loss of income: (Rs.7950/- +10% FP-1/4rd x 12x9) =Rs. 7,08,345/-
Other Heads:-
Loss of filial Consortium-(Rs.44,000X 4) =Rs. 1,76,000/-
 Funeral expenses = Rs.16,
 Loss of Estate = Rs. 16,
----------------------------------------------------------------------
TOTAL =Rs.9,17,345/-
10.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Smt. Badambai vs Raju on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2493538/
2 Rs.9,17,345/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.6,11,600/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.3,05,745/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
11.
